findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the flake-elimination outcome measurable independent of scheduler timing: state that the negative-control (AC3) no longer depends on Python fixture wake-up timing (so it cannot flake by construction), rather than relying on a single full-suite pass to prove non-flakiness.
evidence: Context: 'A 40-minute full suite intermittently classifies the shared dribbling fake remote as stalled'
Evidence section: two separate full suites each failed only after ~11,800+ tests, showing non-determinism
AC5: 'the full default suite passes' — a one-shot check against an intermittent failure
findings.finding: AC5's proving evidence ('the full default suite passes') is a single full-suite run, but the defect under repair is an INTERMITTENT flake that only manifests probabilistically under 40-minute scheduler load. One green suite run cannot durably prove the flake is eliminated — the criterion can pass by luck while the flake persists.
scenarios: The suite passes once post-change, ticket closes, and the flake recurs on a later CI run because the negative-control tests still ride real libcurl timing
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe AC5/Step 5 so the durable proof is structural — e.g. 'the only real-libcurl timing test uses the production 10s window with a transfer whose duration exceeds the window by the empirically-derived margin (>=10.5s pause per experiments), so its outcome is timing-insensitive to fixture delays' — and keep the full-suite run as a confirmatory, not sole, check.

tests/_stall_remote.py line 45 currently computes chunk = b'x' * max(1, rate // 10) with NO cumulative catch-up — step 1 ADDS this mechanism

findings.finding: Step 1 / AC #1 build and extract a cumulative bytes-owed catch-up mechanism (absent from tests/_stall_remote.py today) plus a dedicated pure unit test, but the plan's own Evidence states catch-up alone is insufficient and the Proven-root-cause names the 2s-vs-10s window separation (steps 2-3) as the actual fix — so the catch-up code and its test surface are retained complexity not needed for the done-definition.
scenarios: Reviewer/author invests in building + extracting + unit-testing a catch-up path that the plan already proved does not remove the flake
